en: In a vacuum without air resistance, a heavy bowling ball and a light feather fall at the exact same speed.
Static friction keeps a parked jeepney from sliding down a steep hill even when its wheels are completely stopped.
Magnets attract metals like nickel and cobalt, which is why some Philippine five-peso coins stick to a refrigerator magnet.
A movable pulley attached directly to a heavy box actually halves the effort force you need to lift it.
Holding a cold glass of calamansi juice cools your hand because heat energy flows out of your warm skin.
Sound travels much faster through solid steel train rails than through the air because solid particles are packed tightly.
Sunlight travels through the empty vacuum of outer space to reach Earth without needing any physical medium like air.
A glowing LED bulb transforms electrical energy into light, but the actual electrons flowing through the wire are never consumed.
A boulder resting near the peak of Mount Pulag possesses significant gravitational potential energy purely because of its elevated position.
Using a long crowbar reduces the effort force needed to pry a heavy rock, but the total work done remains unchanged.
If you break a bar magnet perfectly in half, each new piece will still have both a north and south pole.
A skydiver falling through the atmosphere experiences air resistance, which is scientifically classified as a type of fluid friction.
